headline: Timed Entry for Monuments and High-Demand Museums
reservation: While the National Mall is an open public space, specific sites like the Washington Monument and various Smithsonian museums require timed-entry passes. Major federal landmarks including the White House require requests months in advance through official channels; changing security protocols necessitate a direct check of current official guidelines.

days.title: Legislative Landmarks and American Origins
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the U.S. Capitol Visitor Center

stops.name: United States Capitol
stops.detail: Start at the heart of the District to explore the rotunda and the historic halls of Congress.

stops.name: National Museum of American History
stops.detail: View the Star-Spangled Banner and iconic artifacts that define the American experience.

stops.name: Lincoln Memorial
stops.detail: Walk past the Reflecting Pool to stand before the seated figure of Abraham Lincoln.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours for foot travel between Mall sites; conditions vary by crowd size.
days.note: Distances between monuments are often longer than they appear on maps; pace accordingly.

days.title: Artistic Archives and Colonial Charm
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Library of Congress

stops.name: Library of Congress
stops.detail: Observe the intricate mosaics and architectural grandeur of the Thomas Jefferson Building.

stops.name: National Gallery of Art
stops.detail: Transition from classical European masterpieces in the West Building to modern works in the East Building.

stops.name: Georgetown Waterfront Park
stops.detail: Enjoy views of the Potomac River and the historic C&O Canal in this pre-Revolutionary neighborhood.

days.driving: Local transfer via bus or rideshare for Georgetown; allow 20-30 minutes.
days.note: Georgetown is not directly served by the Metro; plan for a walk from Foggy Bottom or use a bus.

days.title: Riverside Remembrance and Green Escapes
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Arlington National Cemetery

stops.name: Arlington National Cemetery
stops.detail: Witness the Changing of the Guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on the Virginia side of the river.

stops.name: U.S. Marine Corps War Memorial
stops.detail: Visit the Iwo Jima statue for a panoramic view of the Washington, D.C. skyline.

stops.name: Smithsonian National Zoo
stops.detail: Explore the diverse habitats in Woodley Park, focusing on global conservation efforts.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for travel across the Potomac; conditions vary with traffic.
days.note: Arlington involves significant uphill walking; consider the interpretive shuttle.

intel.title: Metrorail Convenience
intel.text: Parking is extremely limited and expensive near the National Mall; use the Metrorail system and a SmarTrip card for easier access. Most major monuments are within a short walk of the Smithsonian or L'Enfant Plaza stations.

intel.title: Cellular Connectivity
intel.text: Signal is generally strong throughout the District, though indoor museum galleries may have dead zones. Public Wi-Fi is available in many Smithsonian buildings but may be intermittent during high-occupancy events.

intel.title: Refueling the Vehicle
intel.text: Gas stations are scarce in the downtown core; refuel in Arlington or Silver Spring before entering the city center. Charging stations for electric vehicles are primarily located in paid parking garages.

intel.title: Avoiding the Rush
intel.text: The monuments are open 24 hours but are most crowded during school group hours from 10 AM to 4 PM. Consider visiting the memorials after dusk when they are illuminated and foot traffic decreases.

intel.title: Security Screenings
intel.text: Expect airport-style security at all federal buildings and Smithsonians; large bags are often prohibited. Check the official NPS alerts page for temporary closures due to state events or dignitary visits.

plan.arrival: Collect rental at DCA, then take a 10-minute drive or Metro ride to a downtown hotel for bag drop before visiting the Mall.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient, but public transit is highly recommended over driving within the District due to traffic and restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool for sunset views, though haze varies by season.
